lead: A context-free grammar and a pushdown automaton are two spellings of one idea. The grammar writes rules; the PDA runs them with a stack. This chapter gives both conversion recipes. CFG to PDA uses one working state and keeps the unexpanded part of a leftmost derivation on the stack. PDA to CFG builds variables [p A q] that mean 'go from p to q and remove A'. The pair proves that PDAs accept exactly the context-free languages, the fact every parser relies on.
prereq: You need: 4.1 for the machine and instantaneous descriptions, and Unit 3 for productions, derivations, leftmost derivations and grammar simplification.

sections.h3: From grammar to PDA: one working state and a stack

blocks.text: The stack holds the unexpanded part of a leftmost derivation. Its top is the leftmost symbol still to process. A nonterminal is expanded; a terminal is matched with input.

items: Use one working state q, bottom marker Z₀, and stack alphabet Γ = Σ ∪ V ∪ {Z₀}. Σ is the terminal alphabet; V is the set of variables.
Start by pushing the start symbol S above Z₀: δ(q,ε,Z₀) = {(q, S Z₀)} in top-left transition notation. The figure writes stacks bottom to top, so this is Z₀ S.

For each production A → α, add δ(q,ε,A) = {(q, α)}. In top-left transition notation the leftmost symbol of α is the new top. For S → aSb, push a S b to get stack Z₀ b S a when written bottom to top, with a on top.
For each terminal a, add δ(q,a,a) = {(q,ε)}. It pops a and consumes one input symbol.
Add δ(q,ε,Z₀) = {(q,ε)} to empty the stack after S has been matched. If the grammar does not derive ε, use a separate start state for the first move so this pop cannot happen early.

blocks.text: Each ε-move applies one production to the leftmost nonterminal. Each terminal move matches the next input symbol. The PDA accepts exactly L(G) by empty stack.

sections.h3: From PDA to grammar: variables that pop one stack symbol

blocks.text: First put the PDA in simple form: it accepts by empty stack, and every move either pushes one symbol or pops one symbol. Use 4.2 if it currently accepts by final state.

For states p,q and stack symbol A, make a variable [p A q]. It derives the input strings that take the PDA from state p with A on top to state q with A removed. Removing A also removes everything pushed above it; the stack below A is untouched.

items: Pop: if δ(p,a,A) contains (p′, ε), add [p A p′] → a.

Push: if δ(p,a,A) contains (p′, B₁B₂…Bₖ), k ≥ 1, and B₁ is the new top, add [p A q] → a [p′ B₁ r₁] [r₁ B₂ r₂] … [r_{k-1} Bₖ q] for every state q and all intermediate states r₁,…,r_{k-1}. The first variable pops B₁, the next pops B₂, and so on.

Add a new start symbol S with S → [q₀ Z₀ q] for every state q ∈ Q. q₀ is the start state and Z₀ is the bottom marker. This says: start at q₀ with Z₀, consume the input, and finish in any state with Z₀ gone.

blocks.text: The triple construction creates |Q|²|Γ| variables [p A q], plus the new start symbol S, so |Q|²|Γ| + 1 grammar variables, many useless. Apply the simplification steps from Unit 3 in this order: eliminate ε-productions, then unit productions, then useless variables. The language stays the same.

sections.h3: Why this proves PDAs and CFGs are equally powerful

blocks.text: The first recipe turns any CFG into a PDA, so every context-free language is PDA-accepted. The second turns any PDA into a CFG, so every PDA language is context-free. Together they prove CFL = PDA languages.

The stack in the first direction is a leftmost derivation in progress. In the second direction, each variable [p A q] summarises a whole stack-popping computation. The grammar may be huge, but it is valid.
Parsers use the first direction. A top-down parser predicts productions and keeps expected symbols on a stack. See 4.5 for the parser view.

figure.caption: The stack grows when S expands to aSb and shrinks when terminals match. The marked cell is the top; the stack is written bottom to top.

spec.aria: A six-row array showing the stack growing and shrinking while the one-state PDA expands S and matches a and b on input ab, with the top cell marked in each row.
spec.title: One-state PDA running S → aSb | ε on input ab

examples.question: Use the CFG-to-PDA recipe on G: S → aSb | ε. Build the one-working-state PDA P that accepts L(G) by empty stack. Trace P on input ab. Write the stack after every move, bottom to top, and say whether ab is accepted.
steps: States: {q}; start state q; input alphabet {a,b}; stack alphabet {a,b,S,Z₀}; bottom marker Z₀.
Start move: δ(q,ε,Z₀) = {(q, S Z₀)}. In bottom-to-top display this gives stack Z₀ S.
Production moves: S → aSb gives δ(q,ε,S) ∋ (q, a S b), since α = a S b. S → ε gives δ(q,ε,S) ∋ (q, ε).
Final pop: δ(q,ε,Z₀) = {(q,ε)}. It is safe here because S → ε, so ε is in L(G).

Trace, writing each configuration as (state, input left, stack bottom to top): (q, ab, Z₀) ⊢ (q, ab, Z₀ S) start move ⊢ (q, ab, Z₀ b S a) expand S → aSb ⊢ (q, b, Z₀ b S) match a ⊢ (q, b, Z₀ b) expand S → ε ⊢ (q, ε, Z₀) match b ⊢ (q, ε, ε) pop Z₀.
The input is empty and the stack is empty after six moves, so ab is accepted.
examples.answer: P accepts ab by empty stack; the stack sequence is Z₀S, Z₀bSa, Z₀bS, Z₀b, Z₀, ε.

traps: Pushing αᴿ under top-left transition notation. For A → α write δ(q,ε,A) ∋ (q, α). Pushing αᴿ puts the rightmost symbol of α on top, so the PDA processes the right end first and strings come out reversed.

Forgetting the final pop of Z₀. Without it the stack never empties, so empty-stack acceptance fails. If the grammar does not derive ε, use a separate start state so the pop is not available at time zero.
In PDA-to-CFG, missing intermediate states r_i. The push production must be written for every choice of q and every r₁,…,r_{k-1}; otherwise strings are lost.
Expecting the PDA-to-CFG grammar to be small or clean. It has |Q|²|Γ| + 1 grammar variables and needs the Unit 3 simplification steps.
Mixing the two directions: CFG-to-PDA pushes the production right-hand side α; PDA-to-CFG writes one variable per pushed symbol, not one variable for the whole string.

quiz.q: What does the variable [p A q] mean in the PDA-to-CFG construction?
quiz.a: It derives the strings that take P from state p with A on top to state q with A removed, leaving the stack below A unchanged.

quiz.q: Why push α for a production A → α in the CFG-to-PDA construction?
quiz.a: With top-left transition notation, pushing α puts the leftmost symbol of α on top. Stack displays are written bottom to top, so it appears at the right end of the display. The PDA then works on the leftmost unexpanded symbol first.

quiz.q: Grammar S → 0S1 | ε. Give the production moves for the one-working-state PDA.
quiz.a: δ(q,ε,S) contains (q, 0S1) and (q, ε). Terminal moves are δ(q,0,0) = δ(q,1,1) = {(q,ε)}.

quiz.q: Why does the PDA-to-CFG construction produce useless variables?
quiz.a: It creates [p A q] for every pair of states and every stack symbol, including pairs that no run can connect. Simplification removes them without changing the language.

quiz.q: State the two production forms used in PDA-to-CFG.
quiz.a: Pop: [p A p′] → a for δ(p,a,A) ∋ (p′,ε). Push: [p A q] → a [p′ B₁ r₁] … [r_{k-1} Bₖ q] for δ(p,a,A) ∋ (p′,B₁…Bₖ).

quiz.q: Why is a CFG-to-PDA run a leftmost derivation?
quiz.a: The stack top is always the leftmost unexpanded symbol. Expanding it applies one production; matching a terminal consumes the next input symbol. No later symbol can be expanded first.

quiz.q: For δ(p,a,A) = {(q, BC)}, write the push production form.
quiz.a: [p A r] → a [q B s] [s C r] for all states r and s.

quiz.q: How many variables does PDA-to-CFG create for |Q| = 4 and |Γ| = 3?
quiz.a: It creates |Q|²|Γ| = 4² × 3 = 48 variables of the form [p A q], plus the new start symbol S, so 49 grammar variables before simplification.

beyond: Not for the exam. This construction is the theoretical base of parser generators. LL and LR parsers are deterministic pushdown machines built from grammar productions; GLR and Earley parsers handle nondeterminism. Search for 'CFG to PDA conversion', 'PDA to CFG triple construction' and 'simple PDA normal form' to see implementations and proofs. Modern curricula also connect it to parsing expression grammars and packrat parsing.
